Privacy BayCounty.me doesn't sell, share or track you. There are no ads and no tracking cookies, on the website or in the iPhone and Android apps. The only accounts are for the realtor console. The website Visits. The site counts page views with Vercel Web Analytics, which uses no cookies and doesn't identify you. Email alerts. If you sign up, we keep your email address and what you chose to follow, so we can send the emails. Every email has a link to change or stop them. To have your address deleted entirely, email us. Contact form. Your message, name and email come to us by email so we can answer. They aren't added to any list. API. Requests to the public API are logged with the caller's IP address for 90 days to stop abuse, then deleted. Ask. Questions you type on the Ask page are sent to an AI service to write the answer, along with the public records it looks up. BayCounty.me doesn't save your questions or the answers; it logs only how many were asked (with a scrambled form of your IP address, to enforce limits) and what they cost. Please don't type personal information. Realtor console. Agents who sign in to the realtor console have an account under their email address. We keep the branding they save (name, brokerage, contact details, logo, photo and colors) and the addresses they've run reports for, so they can run them again. A sign-in cookie keeps them signed in for 30 days. None of it is shared or shown to anyone else, and an agent can delete the account, branding and history from the console at any time. Addresses sent to the address report are not logged. My Address. Address lookups go straight from your browser to Bay County's and FEMA's public map servers. BayCounty.me doesn't receive or store what you look up. The iPhone and Android apps No data collected. The app has no accounts, analytics or advertising, and sends nothing about you to BayCounty.me. Your address and location. If you save a home address, it stays on your phone. If you tap "Use my location," the app asks permission first and uses your location once to find your address on Bay County's public map server. It isn't stored or sent anywhere else. Downloaded data. The app saves copies of the public records it shows so it works offline. Deleting the app deletes them. Maps. The Android app draws its maps with OpenStreetMap tiles, so OpenStreetMap's servers see your IP address when they send them, as any website would. The iPhone app uses Apple Maps. Crash reports. If you've allowed it in your phone's settings, Apple or Google may share anonymous crash reports with the developer. Questions Email hello@fluxlabs.net or use the contact form . BayCounty.me is run by Flux Labs in Panama City, Florida.

CRA ledger items that are only proposed or planned stay on the CRA ledger . Payees are matched to the site's vendor list by name. 598 payees are named; grant programs whose recipients aren't named are grouped, and private home addresses are left out. Campaign gifts come from officials' most recent reports and 2026 candidates' reports with the Supervisor of Elections; 49 businesses both gave to a campaign and were paid in these records. A gift and a payment appearing together is a fact about the records. It says nothing about why either happened, and most spending is approved by the full board.

The County Commission, each city commission or council, and the School Board vote on budgets, tax rates and big contracts. Appointed managers run operations. A county manager or city manager, hired by the board, runs departments and staff. Springfield and Parker have no manager; the board oversees staff directly and a city clerk handles administration. Five county officers are elected on their own. The Sheriff, Property Appraiser, Tax Collector, Clerk of Court and Supervisor of Elections each run their own office. The County Commission funds most of their budgets. Their pay is set by a state formula. State auditor reports Florida Auditor General reviews beyond the yearly audit. Operational Audit (period Oct. 2022 - Jan. 2024) (Report No. 2025-095, January 2025) Finding 1. Heavy turnover: from Jan. 2020 to Aug. 2024 the City Administrator position turned over 3 times, City Clerk 2 times, and City Accountant 3 times (vacant 495 days). Records showed allegations of a negative workplace and conflicts between management and elected officials. Finding 2. Audits and annual financial reports were filed late for FY2020-21 through FY2022-23 (FY2021-22 audit was 362 days late). The Department of Revenue withheld $37,137 ($29,166 half-cent sales tax + $7,971 municipal revenue sharing) as of August 2024. Finding 3. Competitive procurement not followed: 5 purchases totaling $564,092 (including $250,000 disaster debris removal, $130,772 fuel from the same local vendor for at least 19 years, $110,260 yard waste) were not competitively selected; other bids/RFPs lacked advertising documentation. Finding 4. 9 purchases totaling $1 million lacked City Council approval required for purchases over $10,000; purchase orders were not used as required, and receipt of goods/services was not always documented. Finding 5. The city paid a contractor the same $450,031 invoice twice; the contractor refunded $328,964 on Dec. 13, 2023 (the duplicate less $121,067 retainage). Finding 6. The city kept paying its contracted City Accountant after the agreement expired (April 2021) and issued 1099s instead of W-2s without documenting why she was treated as an independent contractor. Finding 7. Application security: user access privileges were not limited to what was necessary. Finding 8. IT access was not always promptly removed when no longer needed. Finding 9. No policies for reporting, investigating and communicating known or suspected fraud.
